Argon-gas atomized ZK60 (Mg-5.20Zn-0.33Zr, wt%) powders supplied by Tangshan Weihao Magnesium Powder Co., Ltd., China were used in the present study. The sieved powders with mean particle diameter of 102 mm
compacted at 200 °C under vacuum by slowly increasing the pressure up to 360 MPa in a steel die. The resulting compacts of 48 mm in diameter were preheated for 10 min in die
then extruded at 200, 250, 300 and 350 °C employing an extrusion ratio of 25:1, where the deformed temperature deviation from the preset temperature was within ±2 °C

attributes.morphology: particles at grain boundaries and triple junctions

evidence.quote: the grain boundaries, especially at the triple junction, are still occupied by little white eutectic-phase particles (β-MgZn2) as shown in Fig. 1b
the β phases completely break into small particles that are homogeneously distributed in the matrix
a sparse distribution of β precipitates, approximately 100 nm in size is noted within the grains when T≥300 °C because of the solute supersaturated state in the RS ZK60 powders (Fig. 2f and h)
The grains in the spherically shaped particles are well defined equiaxed with an average size of 8.0 0.2 mm
the bimodal-grained specimen (Fig. 2a) shows a similar yield strength

attributes.morphology: new ultrafine grains or subgrains at serrated grain boundaries

evidence.quote: Partial DRX is also evident in the formation of new ultrafine grains or subgrains at the serrated grain boundaries (arrows in Fig. 2b)
full DRX throughout the material replaces partial DRX, leading to a homogeneous fully recrystallization structure, with the grain shapes becoming more equiaxed (Fig. 2c and h)
a significant increase in the grain size occurs at 300 °C, that is, the mean grain size change from 0.4 mm to 1.4 mm as the T increases from 250 to 300 °C (Fig. 2c and e)

the σ0.2 versus d−1/2 constructed using data in Table 1 strictly follows a Hall–Petch equation, expressed as σ0.2 ¼208.2þ121.5d−1/2, indicating that grain refinement is the primary reason for the high yield stress of PM ZK60 alloys
work hardening induced by numerous forest dislocation accumulations in the unrecrystallized elongated grain may be another strengthening factor

The lack of strain hardening is attributed to decreased dislocation activities and a lack of defect accumulation mechanisms in the UFG structure. In addition, an increased number of grain boundaries also act as dislocation sinks and sources for lattice dislocations, further assisting the dynamic recovery processes

for the sample processed at T≥300 °C, the recovered strain hardening rate is related to the particle-dislocation interaction (Fig. 4), in which the precipitated β particles provide a number of accumulation sources for dislocation under tensile deformation
